function.mechanism: In food, sulfur dioxide/sulfite species exert antimicrobial action and reduce oxidative/browning reactions by reacting with reactive carbonyl compounds and related substrates.

adi.basis: Temporary group ADI of 0.7 mg SO2 eq/kg bw/day (2016) was withdrawn in 2022 follow-up; EFSA used an MOE approach instead.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA follow-up concluded toxicity data gaps remained; temporary ADI was withdrawn and MOE analysis identified concern in high-exposure scenarios.

adi.basis: JECFA group ADI for sulfur dioxide/sulfites reported as 0-0.7 mg/kg bw.

concerns.summary: Sulfite/metabisulfite can trigger bronchoconstriction in sulfite-sensitive asthmatic individuals in challenge/mechanistic studies.
Mouse studies report genotoxicity signals for sodium metabisulfite at high oral doses; relevance to typical dietary exposures remains uncertain.
A rat study reported hippocampal pyramidal neuron loss after chronic sulfite administration.

A large prospective cohort reported positive associations between higher preservative intake (including total sulfites/potassium metabisulfite) and some cancer endpoints, but causality is not established.
In vitro work indicates apoptosis/ROS/autophagy effects of sodium metabisulfite in human fibroblasts, indicating potential cellular stress pathways at tested concentrations.

no_concern_confirmed: IARC currently classifies sulfur dioxide in Group 3 (not classifiable as to carcinogenicity in humans).
A 7-day rat study did not reproduce older severe gastric lesion findings from historical sulfite studies (PMID:27401986).

populations: children with high dietary sulfite intake
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2016 flagged ADI exceedance in high consumers; 2022 follow-up replaced ADI with MOE and identified concern in high-exposure scenarios.

risk_assessment.rationale: E220 remains permitted in major jurisdictions but under significant caveats: EFSA withdrew the temporary ADI due unresolved toxicology uncertainties and high-exposure concern, while FDA/JECFA still allow controlled use. Overall pattern fits approved-with-caveats rather than clearly low-risk or clearly high-risk status.
key_factors: EFSA 2022 withdrew temporary ADI and used MOE framework
High-end exposure concern in EFSA follow-up outputs
FDA GRAS with explicit use restrictions
JECFA numeric ADI remains 0-0.7 mg/kg bw
Evidence of sensitivity in susceptible asthmatics
